content:
I realized that both https://verso.lean-lang.org/ and https://lean-lang.org/ are built with verso (which looks quite nice!), and I'm wondering is there any benefit to moving https://physlib.io/ to verso as well.

I suppose the usual argument is that we can put some interactive examples on there. I do think https://physlib.io/Dependencies is a cool idea and maybe it is possible to generate something more interactive directly through lean?

This is just a random thought, and I appreciate any input on whether people think this is a good/bad idea generally, and if there are any other potential benefits/challenges of doing so.
This topic was moved here from #PhysLib > Physlib website by ZhiKai Pong.

As someone who knows very basic lean, Verso adds expandable proofs, that's nice but if I am serious enough to read them, I would probably go through the actual database in an IDE and work with it, that's my opinion as a viewer of the website. As a backend volunteer to PhysLean, i would ask how much is the effort (and opportunity cost in terms of where those volunteer efforts can be put alternatively ) for this conversion to verso? (I asked Claude and it seems some efforts, don't have estimates of my own though)
I think what might make the difference is if there is some "ready-to-go" template we can take.

Joseph Tooby-Smith said:

I think what might make the difference is if there is some "ready-to-go" template we can take.

There is https://github.com/leanprover/verso-templates and the verso page itself is available at https://github.com/leanprover/verso-website/blob/d2cbe0227c468e29c20b796f4711d87545b9cd7c/Site/FrontPage.lean#L49-L76

So I don't think this will be too difficult with the assistance of some LLM (maybe I'm underestimating the difficulty here).
